description.narrative:
The School of Hard Knocks #NextGenMen programme would facilitate gender transformative engagements amongst men - seeking to attain better attitudes toward gender equality and prevent gender-based violence. The project activities will take place at soccer facilities in the Western Cape province in South Africa, using workshops, interactive sports programmes with trained facilitators (with added psycho-social support for participants) and advocacy campaigns.
Specific activities include: ? 80 educational workshops delivered by Gender Justice practitioners. ? 80 rounds of gender equitable soccer training delivered by SOHK Coaches (weekly soccer play) ? 8 x community wide Gender Justice media campaigns (for each site) ? 1 x National Gender Justice media campaign
Direct project beneficiaries: Change in attitudes correlated with use of violence against women and decreased support for attitudes that encourage men’s use of intimate partner violence among 160 men.
Indirect beneficiaries: Increased discussion about gender equality and non-violent attitudes with 5000 new gender 'allies.'
Other NGOs: Development of an open source Gender Equity through Sport curriculum.
Sustainability: Proof of concept of organisation’s theory of change will lead to further corporate or grant support for the project in the long term.
The strategic objective would be to initiate change in attitudes correlated with use of violence against women and decreased support for attitudes that encourage men’s use of intimate partner violence among 160 men. Overall, the broader strategic objective is to provide awareness about gender-based violence and harmful gender stereotypes and initiate a way for changing these harmful behaviours. The long-term goal in the ‘theory of change’ would be to encourage developing healthy relationships and a more equitable society with healthier gender roles for men and women.
